Random partitions of a tree like a given one

Source: R/damocles_configurations.R
random_regimes.Rd

random_regimes() draws a partition of the edges of tree with the same regimes as regimes and clades of similar size, placed at random: the null partitions of damocles_partition_test(). Each regime other than that of the root is taken as one or more clades, each starting at an edge where the regime changes (as a shift on that branch in BAMM, or a clade with its stem in clade_regimes()); each clade is moved to an edge, drawn at random, whose subtree holds between 1 / tolerance and tolerance times as many edges, from the largest clade to the smallest, so that nested clades stay nested when sizes allow it. Draws in which a later clade covers an earlier one completely are discarded.

Usage

random_regimes(tree, regimes, tolerance = 2, max_overlap = 0.25)

Arguments

tree

A rooted phylo tree.

regimes

Regime of each edge, in the order of tree$edge.

tolerance

Largest ratio between the sizes of a clade and its random replacement.

max_overlap

Largest Jaccard index between the edges of a clade and those of its random replacement, and largest adjusted Rand index between regimes and the random partition, between 0 and 1.

Value

A factor with one regime per edge, with the levels of regimes.

Details

Edges whose subtree largely coincides with the original clade, such as the edge just above it or those of its large daughter clades, give partitions that are nearly the original one. max_overlap excludes them: the Jaccard index between the edges of the original clade and those of its replacement (shared edges over edges in either) must not exceed it. With max_overlap = 1 any edge of the right size can be drawn.

A clade can also be replaced by its complement: when the clade of a regime is one of the two clades at the root, the other one has no edge in common with it but splits the tree in the same way, and the random partition is the original one with the regimes swapped (in trees with a shift in the rate of speciation, the faster clade often holds most of the tree). So max_overlap also bounds the agreement between the whole partitions, measured by the adjusted Rand index between the regimes of the edges (1 for the same partition, whatever the labels; about 0 for unrelated ones); draws above it are discarded.

See also

damocles_partition_test(), clade_regimes().

Examples

set.seed(8)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(30)
reg <- clade_regimes(tr, list(A = ape::Ntip(tr) + 2))
table(reg)
#> reg
#> background          A 
#>         30         28 
table(random_regimes(tr, reg))
#> 
#> background          A 
#>         36         22
